=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:982-997 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: extract_plan_file_path_sets() treats every backticked span in the Files section as a strong path candidate, so non-path spans such as `actions/checkout@v5`, `origin/main`, `owner/repo`, `feature/x` and `application/json` pass _plan_grant_extensionless_candidate(), which accepts `@` through _PLAN_GRANT_SEGMENT_RE (line 815; also lines 873-879, 913-916, 1203-1207), and end up in ungrantable_plan_paths.
  WHY: Plans that used to get a pipeline grant now hold with plan_path_not_grantable and replannable true; the one re-plan usually reproduces the same text, so the plan then needs a human, which regresses a common plan shape (all reviewers rated it MAJOR).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:988-997 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: An unbackticked bullet path such as "- bin/deploy" or "- public/CNAME" arrives only with strong=False, and _PLAN_PATH_TOKEN_RE (lines 690-692) matches only protected prefixes; when the path is missing, is a directory, or no --planning-root is given, it lands in neither `paths` nor `ungrantable`.
  WHY: The pipeline grant is approved without the listed file, and implement's files_touched guard then refuses the commit and latches ai:scope-blocked, which is the exact #9130 stall and contradicts the promise that "a grant never omits the path" (all reviewers rated it MAJOR).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:1197-1218 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The plan_path_not_grantable / replannable hold is evaluated only inside `elif plan_paths:` when the proposed grant would approve; when every listed path is ungrantable (plan_paths empty), or a protected nested extensionless path such as `scripts/deploy` holds as path_not_granted, which _plan_hold_replannable (lines 1112-1124, 1257) treats as not replannable, the hold stays open_grant_not_exact or path_not_granted without replannable true.
  WHY: The poller's #8339 re-plan branch requires gate_replannable == "true", so it never fires and the issue stalls for a human, which contradicts Q4:A ("held as replannable, so it gets one re-plan") (all reviewers rated it MAJOR).
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:1083 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: plan_files_outside_files_touched() adds only tree-verified files, so ungrantable extensionless paths (missing, a directory, or no root) are dropped from the comparison against a human-written files_touched list.
  WHY: A plan that lists `bin/deploy` in the poller (no root), or a new extensionless file in plan.yml, is approved through this gate and then fails implement's guard, which latches ai:scope-blocked.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19585-19657 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The re-plan branch of _plan_auto_approval_gate() now also fires for plan_path_not_grantable, but the /answer body and the Telegram tg_notify_issue text still say the hold came from "directory or glob tokens".
  WHY: The planner is told that a legitimate exact file is a placeholder or directory, so the re-plan can drop or rename a needed file, and operators see the wrong cause; severity disagreement: anthropic rated it MAJOR while gemini, minimax and luna rated it NIT, so the highest is used.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:854-859, 873-875 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: _plan_grant_path() returns shape-valid known bare file names from _PLAN_GRANT_BARE_FILE_RE, such as `Makefile` and `_headers`, before it checks the planning tree.
  WHY: A missing or directory path such as `scripts/Makefile` is granted even with --planning-root and can cover its descendants, contrary to the requirement; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly did not confirm this finding (the allowlist predates the PR).
- tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:2180-2280 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push gate lists tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py under "Failures caused by this change", tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py (new tests at lines 28398-28420) is unverified (timeout), and the CI jobs lint, tests-hooks-and-orchestrator and orchestrate-poll (2) failed on head ba04756a3bd1e88ff624fcff3e002b5b289a74ac.
  WHY: The merge gate stays red, and the new plan_path_not_grantable re-plan flow at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19585-19659 has no passing verification; the failing assertion is not localized.
- CI Run Results:orchestrate-poll (2) log_tail | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Integration fingerprint verification failed during CI, so the [ai-merge-resolve] commit was refused.
  WHY: The reviewer infers a regression in how the orchestrator resolves integration conflicts; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash state that these "FAILED" lines are expected output inside a passing test.
- PR description / commit messages:"Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/9130" | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The PR description uses the auto-close keyword "Closes" against #9130, which the reviewer treats as an ai:orchestrator-tracking issue.
  WHY: This violates §21: on merge the tracking issue would auto-close and stop wave dispatch; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes it ("nothing marks #9130 as a tracking issue").
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:CI tests-hooks-and-orchestrator output on head ba04756a | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The lint reports "PR body:line 1 — auto-close keyword 'Fixes' references ai:orchestrator-tracking issue #2734" and "commit message #2:line 3 — auto-close keyword 'resolved' references ai:orchestrator-tracking issue #2734"; the PR description also contains "Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/9130".
  WHY: This violates §21, since merging would auto-close the tracking issue and stop wave dispatch; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 states that these lint lines are expected output of passing tests (test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py).
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:~744-751 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: triage_transient_rerun() relies only on the attempt-1 gate, so concurrent check_run and workflow_run invocations (.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:686-708) for the same failing run can both POST rerun-failed-jobs.
  WHY: The losing call gets a non-201, logs rerun_refused and files an issue while the accepted re-run is still in flight; the impact is bounded by path=open_head_rerun, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes the race (workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:48-53).
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:~744-751 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The rerun POST status line is parsed with `head -n 1 | tr -d '\r'` and matched against `^HTTP/[^[:space:]]+\ 201`, which breaks if a prefix line, folded header or shim output comes first.
  WHY: A real 201 can be logged as failed/rerun_refused and an issue filed that contradicts the run state; gemini adds that a failure could be misread as success; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 states it fails closed.

  PROBLEM: Every backticked span counts as a strong path candidate, including non-paths such as `actions/checkout@v5`, `origin/main`, `owner/repo`, `application/json` and `feature/x`, so they go on the ungrantable list; before this PR they were ignored.
  WHY: A plan whose Files bullet reads "`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — pin `actions/checkout@v5`" now holds with plan_path_not_grantable, and after one re-plan it goes to a human. Suggested fix: treat a span as strong only when it is the bullet's leading token, or check its first segment against the root.
